items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued September 11 at 3:55PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
items.description:
The areas affected include...
Charleston Harbor...
Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20
NM...

* At 355 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located along a line from 9 NM northwest of
Bulls Bay to 14 NM north of Saint Helena Sound, moving southeast at
10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Rattlesnake Shoal, Charleston Nearshore Reef, Charleston Coastal
Anglers, Air Force Reef, Capers Island Buoy, Capers Reef,
Charleston Harbor Entrance, Crab Bank, Bull Breakers, Castle
Pinkney, Wappoo Cut, Lowcountry Anglers, Bulls Bay, Jimmy Leland
Tug and Kiawah Reef.
items.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 11 at 8:30AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
items.description:
The combination of temperatures warming into the lower to mid 90s
with moderate levels of humidity will produce heat indices near 105
this afternoon across much of the South Carolina Lowcountry and
Southeast Georgia. Those participating in outside September 11th
memorial activities should be prepared for this level of heat and
humidity today.

Scattered showers and thunderstorms will produce relief in some areas
later today. Cloud-to-ground lightning will pose a risk to anyone
caught outdoors. Be prepared to seek shelter should thunderstorms
approach. Remember, When Thunder Roars, Go Indoors!
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sunshine, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Lightning can strike 15 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle should thunderstorms approach.
